newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly higher, follow JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly higher, follow JGBs.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE ended slightly higher on Thursday, following in the wake of Japanese government bond futures.

Key December JGB futures set a new high of 124.42 today. One trust bank trader said the rise was due to news the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau will maintain its current portfolio strategy of putting the heaviest weight on JGBs.
JGBs were also supported by healthy demand for non-JGB cash bond issues, the trader said.
"Euroyen futures are following the moves of JGBs," a city bank trader said.
Otherwise, there have been no fresh factors for Euroyen futures, the trader said.
The June contract moved within a range of 99.22 to 99.26 during the day. Turnover was 63,993 contracts.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market this morning, against a projected shortfall of 190 billion yen, maintaining its neutral money market stance.
The weighted average for Japan's key overnight call rate was likely to remain steady at 0.49 percent, a trader for another trust bank said.
The trader said the fall in the overnight call rate to 0.47 percent from the 0.49 percent seen earlier in the day was due to a decrease in fund demand in the latter portion of the day.
"Much of the trade took place at 0.49 percent... I think the rate declined once market players took care of their funding needs," the trader said.

About 85 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.52 percent. Two-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.50 percent. About 25 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.49 percent. All CD rates were unchanged from the previous day.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday: "For the time being, it is appropriate for us to keep the emphasis on making the basis for an economic recovery more solid."
"I don't think the BOJ governor will be able to say that the economy is on an autonomous recovery for some time yet," the third trader said. --Tokyo Treasury Desk, +81-3-5473-3748
